topic: Part 2 strength-signpost paragraph — verify ISS-2567/ISS-2568 patch (22Hz error + supremum framing)
change_summary: Decider self-applied patch closing ISS-2567 (major) and ISS-2568 (moderate): replaced ‘forces the resonant frequency to ≈22 Hz at every radius’ with ‘forces the resonant frequency to a hard floor of ≈8.77 Hz at the pole, rising monotonically outward — best-case spatial averages land at 22–35 Hz — with no remaining free parameter anywhere to reach the observed 7.83 Hz.’ This c2 review verifies the patch.
our_argument_summary: The signpost routes skimmers to the two strongest Part 2 arguments: §2.9 (V13 coordinate circularity) and §2.1 (Schumann). After patch, the §2.1 pointer now leads with the 8.77 Hz polar-floor supremum bound rising monotonically outward, with the 22–35 Hz spatial averages as supporting detail, matching §2.1’s self-identified strongest argument.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Signpost is navigational intro prose; no code. Underlying physics: f_QW(0)=c/(4·H_max), H_max=H(0)=8,537 km.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: n/a — prose signpost, not a monitored WIN.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: none — signpost makes no code claims.

holes_found.description: Cross-section figure inconsistency for the polar quarter-wave floor f_QW(0). The patched signpost and §2.1 render it as ≈8.77 Hz (13 occurrences total across part2+part6), but part6 contains a single ‘8.78 Hz’ for the SAME quantity (‘f = c/(4H) gives a global minimum of 8.78 Hz at the pole’) while elsewhere part6 itself writes ≈8.77 Hz — so part6 is internally inconsistent (8.77 vs 8.78 for f_QW(0)). NOT introduced by this patch: the signpost correctly inherited the dominant 8.77 convention from §2.1. Surfaced here via the cross-section consistency lens because an arithmetic-auditing defender comparing the signpost’s 8.77 against part6’s 8.78 would see a 0.01 Hz mismatch in a section whose whole rhetorical anchor is ‘contested arithmetic’.
holes_found.recommendation: Harmonize on a single value across part2 + part6. Note the mathematically-correct two-decimal rounding of c/(4·8,537) is 8.78 Hz (8.7792 with c=299,792.458 km/s; 8.785 with the site’s shown c≈300,000), so 8.78 is the more defensible figure — but 8.77 is established in 13 places, so the low-churn fix is to change the one part6 ‘8.78’ to 8.77. Decider’s call; the signpost itself needs no edit.

holes_found.description: ‘best-case spatial averages land at 22–35 Hz’ applies the modifier ‘best-case’ to a range. The most dome-favorable (lowest) spatial average is the linear-radial ≈22.6 Hz; 35 Hz is the area-weighted (least favorable) average. Calling a 22–35 Hz span ‘best-case’ is slightly loose — strictly the best case is the 22 Hz lower bound. Meaning is clear (no averaging scheme reaches 7.83 Hz) and this is intro prose, so impact is cosmetic.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: ‘even the most dome-favorable spatial average still lands at ≈22 Hz (area-weighting pushes it to 35 Hz)’. Low priority — do not block.

The erroneous ‘≈22 Hz at every radius’ constancy claim is fully removed (0 residual occurrences of ‘≈22 Hz at’ in sections.json), and the surviving ‘at every radius’ string is now only the CORRECT part6 usage (‘above 7.83 Hz at every radius’, true under monotonicity) (data/sections.json:arr[8]). Both ISS-2567 (major) and ISS-2568 (moderate) are closed-fixed in monitor/decisions/closed-issues.json. Arithmetic re-verified: c/(4·8,537)=8.78 Hz polar floor; linear-radial H_eff≈3,316 km→f≈22.6 Hz; area-weighted≈35 Hz — all consistent with the signpost’s 8.77-floor / 22–35-average framing (SEC-part2-EXP-579-signpost.c1.json holes 0–1).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: n/a — this is our own review prose, and the patch strengthens it. The verification confirms the signpost now accurately summarizes §2.1 rather than contradicting it; the only residual findings are pre-existing minor cross-section rounding nits (this review holes_found[0–1]), neither of which lives in the patched signpost itself.
